title: TSPO-PET and MRI Imaging as Novel Imaging Tools for Autoimmune Epilepsy
text:
About 5% of focal epilepsy is associated with neural autoantibodies and may respond to immune-modulating
treatment, but the diagnosis of autoimmune epilepsy remains limited to neural autoantibody testing. In this
proposal, we explore novel PET and MR imaging methods that can visualize and quantify microglial activation
and blood brain barrier disruption in people with definite autoantibody positive autoimmune epilepsy, and
clinically suspected but antibody negative focal epilepsy. These studies may improve the diagnosis of
autoimmune epilepsy, explore its neuroinflammatory mechanisms, and develop more broadly applicable
markers of disease that may be used in the context of treatment.

title: Investigating the hydraulic regulation of human gastrulation and mesodermal patterning using stem cells
text:
Investigating the Hydraulic Regulation of Human Gastrulation and Mesodermal
Patterning Using Stem Cells
Project Narrative
This research investigates how mechanical forces due to cavity fluid pressure and tissue
shape, regulate early human embryonic development, focusing on mesoderm induction
and patterning. By improving our understanding of the fundamental biomechanical cues
that drive gastrulation and early body axis formation, this work can provide critical insights
into early pregnancy loss, congenital disorders, and infertility. These findings have the
potential to inform novel strategies for improving reproductive health, prenatal care, and
stem cell-based regenerative medicine, aligning with NICHD’s mission to enhance
maternal and child health outcomes.

title: mHealth-CArdiac REhabilitation for INOCA (INOCA-CARE)
text: Patients with a condition called ischemia with no obstructive coronary artery disease (INOCA) have symptoms including chest pain, fatigue, and depression, and there are currently few effective treatment options. Cardiac rehabilitation, which is an organized way to deliver exercise and lifestyle counseling, has the potential to work for these patients but there are many factors that can make participation difficult (for example, if there are no facilities nearby). Our study will test whether a new platform for cardiac rehabilitation, delivered by an electronic tablet device paired with weekly remote counseling (known as mobile health cardiac rehabilitation), will improve how INOCA patients feel after 3, 6, and 12 months.

title: Immunomodulatory effects of desmoglein 3 chimeric autoantibody receptor T cells (DSG3-CAART) in mucosal pemphigus vulgaris
text:
Current therapies for autoimmune disease chronically suppress the immune system, which risks severe
infection. DSG3-CAART is the first precision T cell immunotherapy for autoimmune disease to enter clinical
trials, which presents a unique opportunity to investigate the immunomodulatory effects of this novel targeted
therapeutic approach in humans. The proposed studies will elucidate the cellular and molecular determinants
of DSG3-CAART activity and host immune response, using clinical samples collected from subjects enrolled in
the DSG3-CAART phase 1 study.

title: CRISPR Tiling
text:
Fusion oncoproteins (FOs) enclose functional elements that drive oncogenic transformation. Core 2 will 
dissect the roles of folded domains and intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) within FOs controlling 
malignant cell proliferation using the high-resolution CRISPR tiling strategy. The technology provided 
by Core 2 will directly support Projects 1, 2, and 3 and contribute to a broader understanding of how 
FOs control condensate formation and oncogenic programs in cancers.

title: Preconditioning brain white matter against ischemia
text:
A growth in the aging population together with improved stroke care has resulted in an increase
in survivors and a rise in recurrent ischemic events. Ischemic preconditioning has been shown to
effectively protect neurons, while mechanisms of preconditioning in white matter remain to be
studied even though axonal injury during stroke underlies the consequent neurological disability
in surviving patients. We propose that inhibiting CK2 using an FDA-approved drug, CX-4945
(Silmitasertib), rapidly preconditions WM against ischemia by targeting axonal mitochondria and
improving functional recovery in young and old WM both in males and females.

title: Microphysiological platform for analyzing multiple myeloma's tumor microenvironment, enabling immunotherapy assessment and drug screening.
text:
Cancer is a leading cause of death around the world. An immune-based, non-toxic approach that attacks the
cancer as well as the supporting deficiencies that facilitate its progression would be a great boon to the field.
This project aims to improve public health by developing a successful tumor immunology model, which can be
applied to study immunological reactions to the immunotherapy and eliminate long-term cancer reappearance
without disrupting normal immune function.

title: Multicomponent hydrogels activating wound-induced hair neogenesis for scarless wound healing.
text:
Scarring in the skin is associated with significant morbidity and characterized by the loss of the hair
follicle, which has crucial roles in regeneration. In mice, wounds can heal with hair follicle regeneration
without scarring through a unique pathway known as wound-induced hair neogenesis. The objective of
this research is to engineer a complex hydrogel system that releases two important, sequential signals
to mimic the biology of wound-induced hair neogenesis as a mechanism to prevent and treat human
skin scars.

title: Developing Robust Multimodal AI for Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma Prognosis
text:
Our proposed research aims to develop advanced artificial intelligence models that can automatically and
robustly predict the progression of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), with a focus on ensuring usability and
seamless integration into clinical practice. By applying state-of-the-art data science techniques, this work will
enhance understanding and management of POAG within ophthalmology. Addressing the shortage of
experienced glaucoma specialists, the proposed tools will enable timely and accurate risk assessment,
supporting earlier interventions to prevent vision loss caused by POAG.

title: Behavior Core
text: Behavior Core Long-term (days to months) and continuous (24 hours/day, 7 days/week) behavioral monitoring of mouse socio- spatial behavior is fundamental to this BRAIN Initiative proposal on “Oxytocin Modulation of Neural Circuit Function and Behavior”. Each Project requires behavioral assessment of mice in home cages or in larger more complex environments, often longitudinally and in conjunction with neural recordings, optogenetics, or other manipulations of cellular and network-level activity. A number of recent technical advances across levels now enable a deeper understanding of neuromodulation on flexible information processing and behavior in mice. Some of these innovations have been pioneered by our laboratories and the Projects/Cores of the Oxytocin U19 in the previous funding cycle. Specifically, it is now possible- if not routine- to apply advanced machine learning and computer vision methods for quantitative behavioral analysis of animal poses and trajectories from video data. This includes video tracking of multiple animals interacting, from different camera angles, across the light/dark cycle, and with simultaneous neural recordings. Over the last five years we have developed hardware, software, and other infrastructure to perform this continuous behavioral monitoring in our facility. Our successes have led to considerable investment in space and computer storage for this facility by NYU Langone. We now capitalize on the development of this facility and behavioral monitoring system to support the next-generation studies of multi-animal behavior and modulation of neural circuit function by the Oxytocin U19 teams. Aim 1 is to improve our capacity for behavioral home cage monitoring, both in terms of number of animals monitored per cage and the pipeline for data collection and analysis. Aim 2 is to develop more complex housing environments for studies of socio-spatial behavior and decision-making in mouse colonies of small to moderate sizes. Aim 3 is to provide a suite of additional social, spatial and other oxytocin-related testing available to Project teams and assisted by Behavior Core staff, including breeding and housing the set of transgenic mouse lines required for this U19 proposal.

title: Membrane-inspired lipid nanoparticles for cell-type-specific expression of programmable RNA
text:
The goal of this proposal is to engineer lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) inspired by natural cell membranes to
achieve precise, cell-type-specific delivery of programmable RNA, thereby enhancing targeted gene
expression in desired cell populations. By combining bio-inspired lipid formulations with RNA-based sensors
that respond to endogenous cellular markers, we aim to overcome the limitations of current viral and non-viral
delivery systems, including immunogenicity and limited specificity. Successful development of these advanced
LNPs will provide scalable, low-immunogenicity gene delivery platforms with unparalleled specificity, advancing
both fundamental biological research and the development of precision molecular therapies.

title: Development of a Universal Next Generation T Cell Receptor Cancer Therapy: Preclinical Proof-of-Concept and Optimization
text:
Cancer is the leading cause of death in many states and the second leading cause of death in the
United States. Despite remarkable initial progress in treating certain leukemias and lymphomas with a
patient's own immune cells, most patients with solid tumors, the most common cancers, as well as
certain blood cancer, such as acute myeloid leukemia, still do not benefit from this form of therapy
because few immune cells penetrate the tumor and most show only transient antitumor activity. Using
a patient's own T cells, we are developing a novel, genetically engineered form of cellular
immunotherapy that overcomes multiple impediments to conventional cell-based therapy.

title: Career Enhancement Program
text: ABSTRACT – CAREER ENHANCEMENT PROGRAM The Cancer Health Disparities SPORE in Endometrial Cancer Career Enhancement Program (CEP) supports research activities for oncology clinicians, oncology clinician scientists, and basic, translational, and clinical scientists with strong interest in cancer health disparities and endometrial cancer research. The SPORE leadership is committed to increasing the pool of endometrial cancer researchers. Each year the CEP will fund 2 CEP investigators from a total of $100,000 in SPORE and matched Institutional funds. We will recruit faculty with an existing endometrial cancer science focus; or have existing health disparities research expertise that is newly being applied to the endometrial cancer context to expand the field. The Cancer Health Disparities SPORE in Endometrial Cancer CEP will provide a rigorous mentorship program for all awardees and a broad ongoing evaluation of their progress. The SPORE and CEP additionally provide fiscal administration, biostatistics and bioinformatics input, biospecimens, genomics and pathology expertise; patient perspective and integration with community outreach activities; mentorship and critical analysis and constructive feedback on progress via CEP advisory board meetings.

title: Knowledge-empowered Lifespan Neuroimage Analysis
text:
This project is dedicated to creating and disseminating the first lifespan-dedicated pipeline for accurate and
consistent processing and analysis of large-scale multimodal lifespan brain MRIs from multiple imaging sites.
We will develop novel knowledge-empowered deep learning techniques for lifespan atlas construction, skull
stripping, artifact correction, super resolution, harmonization, tissue segmentation, topological correction, and
brain labeling. We will freely release our developed pipeline, lifespan atlases, and our processed lifespan data
(50,000+ lifespan subjects with 150,000+ scans), to the public.

title: Convergent allergen-specific antibodies in food allergy
text:
Peanut and tree nut allergy is increasing in prevalence and poses a significant public health risk, as
patients can develop life-threatening reactions. Antibodies that can bind to allergens underlie both
clinical reactions to food allergens and tolerance after treatment. Our project focuses on
understanding how these allergens are recognized by antibodies in similar ways by many allergic
patients to contribute to our understanding of how food allergies begin and how we can develop new
targeted therapies.

title: University of New Mexico Cancer Center Support Grant
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE • OVERALL
Designated as one of the nation’s National Cancer Institute Cancer Centers since 2005, with comprehensive
designation in 2015, the University of New Mexico Comprehensive Cancer Center is a cancer treatment,
research, and education and training center that applies the scientific expertise of its investigators to those
cancers that have high incidence, mortality, or differences in cancer outcomes as well as healthcare gaps in the
unique populations of New Mexico. The Center is a hub for promoting discovery through its research, education
and training, clinical care, statewide outreach programs and networks for community participatory research to
assure that all the people in New Mexico, its catchment area, have access to high quality cancer care. The
Center connects scientists, healthcare professionals, and communities to translate its discoveries to cancer
clinical trials, and cancer control and behavioral interventions that reduce the cancer burden of New Mexico and
serves as a national model.

title: Identification of cellular functions involved in Hepatitis B Virus infection via a novel RNA sensing and editing dependent reporter system
text:
Lay Statement
Lack of curative therapeutics predisposes the 254 million people living with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection to
substantially increased risk of developing liver cirrhosis and liver cancer that account for 1.1 million deaths per year.
Development of new antivirals has been hampered by the lack of HBV reporter virus system which is critical to enable
unbiased genetic and chemical screening campaigns. This project aims to leverage our novel HBV reporter and implement
the most comprehensive genetic screens to date, to search for still elusive virus-host interactions crucial in maintaining HBV
persistence, a key step toward identifying new targets for curative antiviral therapy.

title: Oral microbial community structure and assembly: from molecule to microbiome
text:
The accumulation of dental plaque into stable, long-range biofilms at the gingival margin is implicated in
reversible gingivitis, which may progress to chronic periodontitis. However, the specific cells and molecular
interactions that govern dental plaque structure are not well known. The knowledge gained from the research
proposed here will comprise a holistic understanding of oral community assembly processes and physical
structure across spatial scales and may identify new paradigms for intervening in the progression of dental
plaque-mediated diseases.

title: Non-coding RNAs in resilience to Alzheimer’s Disease
text:
There are still no effective drugs to treat Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, there are resilient
people who have evidence of disease pathology without displaying cognitive decline. Non-
coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are powerful regulators of coding and non-coding gene expression,
critical for maintaining homeostasis, resisting cellular stresses, and preventing disease
processes. Here we systematically identify ncRNAs that regulates the resilience in AD using
comparative transcriptomic analysis, explore the regulatory mechanisms these ncRNAs in
neural cells, and validate their protective roles using advanced three-dimensional human neural
cell culture models of AD. If successful, future trials on safe-to-use non-coding RNAs could be
performed to protect humans against Alzheimer’s disease.

title: ImpACT: Improving Treatment Strategies for Anaplastic Thyroid Cancer Through Integration of Novel Therapies and Assessment of Tumor Response
text:
Overall
Anaplastic thyroid cancers (ATC) are among the most aggressive solid tumors, characterized by a nearly 100%
mortality rate and a median overall survival of just 3-5 months. While recent advances with kinase inhibitors have
extended survival for some patients, drug resistance inevitably develops, leading to early mortality for all affected
individuals. The primary goal of this P01 Program is to enhance the therapeutic ratio for ATC patients by
exploring innovative hypotheses using cutting-edge methodologies, potentially transforming the clinical
management of this devastating disease.
